title: Washer suspension design and dynamic balancing
short: GD&T schemes and technical specifications for three suspension subsystems, plus counterweight sizing to hold the sub-washer at its operating tilt. The design phase closed with a theoretical factor of safety above 2.
lede: A front-load washer tub has to stay in its operating position while the drum spins. I designed suspension components, specified them with GD&T, and sized the counterweights that set the balance.

stat.label: Theoretical factor of safety at the end of the design phase

ownership: I developed the GD&T schemes and technical specifications for three suspension subsystems, released the drawings in Creo, and managed part configurations in Windchill PLM. I also did the counterweight calculations and placement described below.

results.label: Factor of safety at the end of the design phase
Suspension subsystems with GD&T schemes (ASME Y14.5-2009) and technical specifications
Consistent centroid placement relative to the center of rotation

sections.heading: Problem and constraints
paras: Two connected objectives. The suspension had to control vibration and system dynamics while keeping the tub within its required operating position. Separately, the sub-washer had to be held at its required operating tilt, which is set by where mass sits relative to the center of rotation.

sections.heading: Approach: suspension
bullets: Designed suspension components using machine-elements principles and factor-of-safety analysis.
Developed drawings and schematics with GD&T for manufacturing and assembly, with schemes to ASME Y14.5-2009 and technical specifications for three subsystems.
Evaluated spring placement and load paths to optimize the tub-to-spring interaction and system behavior.

sections.heading: Approach: dynamic balancing
bullets: Calculated counterweight mass, density, and placement.
Determined weight locations that achieve the required center of gravity and tilt angle.
Calibrated the counterweights around the rotating assembly.

sections.heading: Verification
paras: Suspension performance improvements were validated against legacy designs through testing, to support design decisions. The factor of safety above 2 is a theoretical result from the design-phase analysis, not a test measurement.

sections.heading: Results
bullets: Completed the design phase with a theoretical factor of safety above 2.
Established suspension geometry and component designs that meet the required operating conditions.
Achieved consistent centroid placement relative to the center of rotation across all models.
